summary: register() falls back to the target's default mode instead of the mode saved in the ledger. `gstack-harness auto` (setup run inside OpenClaw) and `./setup --host openclaw` therefore switch a user's `--skills all` registration back to router mode and delete the per-skill copies; `refresh` keeps the saved mode, so the paths disagree.
evidence: `const mode = opts.mode ?? t.defaultMode;` with bin/gstack-harness:123 `register({ ...base, target: TARGETS[n], registry: true })` (no mode). Scratch repro: register(dots, mode:'all') -> 'first all 61'; register again without mode -> 'rerun router updated'.

summary: The `same` short-circuit ignores the context file, so re-registering with a different `--context` skips the ledger rewrite. The ledger keeps the old file, the block goes into the new one, and unregister/uninstall leaves the new block pointing at a deleted router.
evidence: Repro: register(generic, skillsDir, context:A) then context:B -> 'status unchanged ledger blocks [".../A.md"]'; after unregister, B still contains '<!-- gstack:begin harness-routing -->' and 'router exists false'.

summary: With `--context` and `--skills all` there is no router, and contextBlock(router ?? '') writes a block that tells the agent to read an empty path.
evidence: Repro: register(generic, mode:'all', context) -> 'router null' and the block text 'read ``, pick the one skill whose line matches'.

summary: When the mode changes, files that are no longer wanted are deleted but their folders are not, leaving empty skill folders in the harness's skills folder until uninstall.
evidence: After the all->router repro: `find sk -type f` shows only gstack/SKILL.md; `find sk -type d -empty | wc -l` -> 61.

summary: The ledger is written only after every payload file is written. If a first registration is interrupted part way, the files are on disk but unrecorded: a retry fails with HARNESS_UNOWNED_ENTRY on gstack's own files, and gstack-uninstall cannot remove them.
evidence: Write loop at lines 441-455 (`fs.writeFileSync(p + '.gstack-new', b)` at 452) runs before `writeLedger(lfile, {...})` at 456; the ownership check at 416-419 throws HARNESS_UNOWNED_ENTRY for any existing top-level entry not in the previous ledger.

summary: The test compares the whole fixture <home>/.claude before and after setup, so it fails whenever anything other than the harness auto-registration writes into <home>/.claude during the run. It failed here when a Claude Code telemetry file appeared in between, while the real `claude` binary was on PATH.
evidence: `bun test test/harness-register.test.ts ...` -> 143 pass, 1 fail: '+ "1p_failed_events.78d147bd-....json"' in tree(f.home/.claude); `which claude` -> /usr/local/bin/claude; the fixture PATH appends process.env.PATH (test/helpers/install-fixture.ts:182).

summary: The context-block remover deletes everything from the first begin marker to the next end marker, or to the end of the file if there is none. insertBlock appends a new block instead of fixing an orphaned begin marker, so uninstall deletes user-written lines between the old begin marker and the new block.
evidence: File 'top / <!-- gstack:begin harness-routing --> / old gstack text / USER NOTES I WROTE / more user text'; ran insertBlock(contextBlock('/x/SKILL.md')) then _gstack_harness_cut_block; the file afterwards contained only 'top'.

summary: When the payload is unchanged (same=true), register skips writeLedger, so meta.version never updates. status reports the registration stale forever and 'gstack-harness refresh' cannot clear it.
evidence: Scratch script: register dots at version 1.0.0.0, register again at 2.0.0.0 -> 'unchanged'; status -> [["1.0.0.0",true]]; after refresh(): still [["1.0.0.0",true]].

summary: setup's harness arm runs 'gstack-harness register <host>' without --skills, and --refresh-registered re-runs './setup --host openclaw' for registered rows. That resets a user's '--skills all' OpenClaw registration to router mode on every upgrade.
evidence: register() uses opts.mode ?? t.defaultMode. Scratch run: register(mode:'all') -> 'all 61'; register() with no mode on the same dest -> 'router updated router' (ledger meta.mode router).

summary: For the generic target with --skills all and --context, router is null, so contextBlock(router ?? '') writes a routing block telling the agent to read an empty path.
evidence: register({target: generic, mode:'all', context}) wrote: 'For a coding, review, test, plan or release task, read ``, pick the one skill...'.
